parts.text: Is he working like a scientist on this daily-life problem?

options.text: Yes, because he observes, tries a change, and can check whether the drip slows.
No, because a dripping tap is not a problem science can touch.
Yes only if he already knows the exact name of every part of the tap.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Dhruv's tap drips. He puts a bowl under it, notes how fast it fills, and tries tightening the handle.

part_answers.answer: He observes, tries a change, and can check the result, so he is using the scientific method on a daily-life problem.

teacher.key_rationale: Working like a scientist means using the scientific method — observe, try a change, check the result — even on a household drip. Naming every part or writing a report first is not required.
